name: Mock community taxonomic profiling benchmark (Portik et al. 2022)
description: Eleven profiling methods (14 configurations) on PacBio HiFi, ONT and Illumina reads from ATCC and ZymoBIOMICS mock communities, scored on species detection and abundance.

attributes.task: Species-level presence detection and relative abundance estimation in mock microbial communities
attributes.source_locator: Tables 1-4; Methods 'Detection metrics' and 'Relative abundance estimates'

limitations: Mock communities of cultured organisms without human host DNA; not clinical specimens.

name: control_signal_and_optimisation: dna-pathogen-20261009-protocol-song2025-bsi-vgs-abundance
description: Descriptive fact transcribed from the pinned source.

attributes.value: BLAST was the only software that detected viridans group streptococci in all five culture-positive samples, but it also gave signal in the negative blood and no-template control. Lowering the BLAST e-value to 10E-13 removed reads from both controls while all culture-positive samples stayed positive (Figure 1). Removing human reads first did not change viridans streptococci abundances (p = 0.15).

name: Relative abundance of viridans group streptococci in culture-positive patient blood and negative controls (Song et al. 2025 Table 2)
description: Each pipeline's relative abundance of viridans group streptococci in five culture-positive blood metagenomes and in negative blood and no-template controls.

attributes.protocol: Blood culture is the reference. For each sample, report the relative abundance of viridans group streptococci assigned by each pipeline; the same read-out in negative blood and no-template control shows contamination or false-positive signal. The study counts a detection as valid only if absent from both negative controls.
attributes.version: Table 2 (pipelines at the settings in Methods 'Data Analysis'; before the BLAST e-value optimisation shown in Figure 1)
attributes.source_locator: Methods 'Data Analysis' paragraph 1; Results paragraph 2; Table 2
limitations: Five culture-positive samples, all viridans group streptococci; no culture-negative patient samples analysed.
Table 2 prints relative abundances, not detection calls; the study's validity rule (absent from both controls) is applied in the text.
BLAST e-value optimisation that removed control signal is reported only in Figure 1, not in a table.

limitations: One positive-control library; no replicates.

evidence_concerns.message: Table 1 prints Kraken relative abundances of 5.17E‐10 (Salmonella enterica and Escherichia coli), 5.17E‐11 (Lactobacillus fermentum) and 5.17E‐12 (Enterococcus faecalis): one mantissa over three orders of magnitude. name: Relevance of M. tuberculosis read classification, real Illumina (Hall and Coin 2024 Table 8) to "Select a DNA pathogen-identification workflow for diagnostic testing"
description: Comparing standard and pathogen-focused databases on reads of known origin measures how reference completeness changes identification of a clinically relevant pathogen, which bears on the use case's question about organisms poorly represented in the reference. It is proxy evidence: read-level classification of one pathogen in constructed metagenomes, not sample-level diagnosis.

attributes.endpoint: Per-read sensitivity, specificity and Youden's index (95% Wilson intervals), throughput and peak memory for kraken and minimap2 with three databases each, classifying M. tuberculosis reads in a real Illumina sputum-like metagenome
attributes.rationale: Comparing standard and pathogen-focused databases on reads of known origin measures how reference completeness changes identification of a clinically relevant pathogen, which bears on the use case's question about organisms poorly represented in the reference. It is proxy evidence: read-level classification of one pathogen in constructed metagenomes, not sample-level diagnosis.
constraints: Inspect every linked evaluation's source locator and preserved limitations before citing a result.
Do not combine these results with another protocol's results; datasets, databases and scoring rules differ between sources.
limitations: Read-level, not sample-level, metrics; one target pathogen.
Constructed metagenomes (simulated or mixed real reads), not patient specimens.
Three configurations use databases built by the authors (author_reported).

Only the kraken Myco database is stated to exclude the genomes used to simulate reads. Whether the 17 M. tuberculosis references in the minimap2 MTB, Clockwork and Myco databases include the simulated lineage 1 assembly or the strain behind the real M. tuberculosis reads (ERR245682, ERR8170871) is not stated, so overlap with the truth set may favour those configurations (Methods 'Mycobacterium read classification').

Kraken with the standard databases misses most M. tuberculosis reads at species rank, but at least 90% of those misses are correct at genus level (Results 'Real Illumina' paragraph 3), so species-level read sensitivity understates genus-level detection.

name: Relevance of HiFi ATCC MSA-1003 mock community (PacBio Sequel II HiFi): species detection at 0.001% of total reads (Portik et al. 2022 Table 4) to "Select a DNA pathogen-identification workflow for diagnostic testing"
description: Counting false-positive species and missed species in a mock community of known composition measures how a classification workflow handles spurious low-abundance calls and detection, which bears on the use case. It is proxy evidence because the samples are mock communities of cultured organisms without host DNA, not clinical specimens.

attributes.endpoint: Species-level true and false positives, false negatives, precision, recall, F1, F0.5 and abundance L1 error for 14 classification configurations on PacBio HiFi, ATCC MSA-1003 mock community reads
attributes.rationale: Counting false-positive species and missed species in a mock community of known composition measures how a classification workflow handles spurious low-abundance calls and detection, which bears on the use case. It is proxy evidence because the samples are mock communities of cultured organisms without host DNA, not clinical specimens.
constraints: Inspect every linked evaluation's source locator and preserved limitations before citing a result.
Do not combine these results with another protocol's results; datasets, databases and scoring rules differ between sources.
limitations: Mock community of cultured organisms without human host DNA or a clinical specimen matrix.
Each method used its own reference database (Table 2), so method and database effects are confounded.
Single run per dataset; no intervals.
Sourmash rows are reported by sourmash authors (author_reported); the first author is a PacBio employee and MEGAN-LR workflows are PacBio's.

Detection uses the authors' threshold of 0.001% of total reads (Methods 'Detection metrics' paragraph 1, Table 3); the authors note it penalises methods that assign fewer reads, and report that a 0.1% threshold cut short-read false positives from several hundred to about 10 or fewer (Results 'Detection metrics' paragraph 5).
Two co-authors (C. T. Brown, N. T. Pierce-Ward) wrote the cited sourmash papers and Pierce-Ward ran the analysis; the competing-interests statement does not declare this.

name: Relevance of Illumina ZymoBIOMICS D6300 standard (NovaSeq 6000), subsampled: species detection at 0.001% of total reads (Portik et al. 2022 Table 4) to "Select a DNA pathogen-identification workflow for diagnostic testing"
description: Counting false-positive species and missed species in a mock community of known composition measures how a classification workflow handles spurious low-abundance calls and detection, which bears on the use case. It is proxy evidence because the samples are mock communities of cultured organisms without host DNA, not clinical specimens.

attributes.endpoint: Species-level true and false positives, false negatives, precision, recall, F1, F0.5 and abundance L1 error for 7 classification configurations on Illumina, Zymo D6300 mock community reads
attributes.rationale: Counting false-positive species and missed species in a mock community of known composition measures how a classification workflow handles spurious low-abundance calls and detection, which bears on the use case. It is proxy evidence because the samples are mock communities of cultured organisms without host DNA, not clinical specimens.
constraints: Inspect every linked evaluation's source locator and preserved limitations before citing a result.
Do not combine these results with another protocol's results; datasets, databases and scoring rules differ between sources.
limitations: Mock community of cultured organisms without human host DNA or a clinical specimen matrix.
Each method used its own reference database (Table 2), so method and database effects are confounded.
Single run per dataset; no intervals.
Sourmash rows are reported by sourmash authors (author_reported); the first author is a PacBio employee and MEGAN-LR workflows are PacBio's.
Only short-read and general methods were run on the Illumina data.

Detection uses the authors' threshold of 0.001% of total reads (Methods 'Detection metrics' paragraph 1, Table 3); the authors note it penalises methods that assign fewer reads, and report that a 0.1% threshold cut short-read false positives from several hundred to about 10 or fewer (Results 'Detection metrics' paragraph 5).
Two co-authors (C. T. Brown, N. T. Pierce-Ward) wrote the cited sourmash papers and Pierce-Ward ran the analysis; the competing-interests statement does not declare this.

name: Relevance of Viridans streptococci in culture-positive blood and negative controls (Song et al. 2025 Table 2) to "Select a DNA pathogen-identification workflow for diagnostic testing"
description: Real patient blood with a blood-culture reference and negative controls is the use case's setting, and the control rows show contamination signal. It is held as proxy because the table reports relative abundances rather than detection calls, covers five samples of one organism group, and has no culture-negative patients.

attributes.endpoint: Relative abundance of viridans group streptococci assigned by BLAST, Kraken, RTG Core and MetaPhlAn in five blood-culture-positive patient blood metagenomes, a negative blood control and a no-template control
attributes.rationale: Real patient blood with a blood-culture reference and negative controls is the use case's setting, and the control rows show contamination signal. It is held as proxy because the table reports relative abundances rather than detection calls, covers five samples of one organism group, and has no culture-negative patients.
constraints: Inspect every linked evaluation's source locator and preserved limitations before citing a result.
Do not combine these results with another protocol's results; datasets, databases and scoring rules differ between sources.
limitations: Five culture-positive samples, all viridans group streptococci; no culture-negative patient samples.
Relative abundances, not detection calls; the study's control-based validity rule is applied in the text.
BLAST's later e-value optimisation (Figure 1) is not in the table and was not extracted.
Kraken and MetaPhlAn versions and databases unreported.

The study counts a detection as valid only if it is absent from both negative controls (Methods 'Data Analysis'). BLAST gives 1.03E‐1 in negative blood and 2.59E‐1 in the no-template control, above four of the five patient samples, so none of its Table 2 assignments meets that rule. The Abstract, Discussion and Conclusion statements of complete concordance refer to a later run with a stricter e-value, shown only in Figure 1.
DNA was extracted from 200 µL of whole blood with host-DNA depletion and whole-genome amplification (Methods 'Sample Collection and Processing'), not plasma cell-free DNA as in the use case's inputs.
The same source carries an evidence concern about its Table 1 Kraken values, which withholds this judgement until it is resolved.

attributes.endpoint: Relative abundance of eight species in a log-distributed mock standard (8.9E-1 to 8.9E-7) for BLAST, MetaPhlAn, RTG Core and Kraken, against the theoretical distribution

constraints: Inspect every linked evaluation's source locator and preserved limitations before citing a result.

limitations: One positive-control library; no replicates or intervals.
Abundances, not detection calls; no threshold applied in the table.

Table 1 lists eight bacteria whose theoretical abundances sum to 0.990; Results paragraph 1 says the standard also contains yeasts, which the table omits.
